title: How to Handle Doubt
excerpt: Doubt is not the opposite of faith. Often it is the growing pains of a faith outgrowing the answers it was handed as a child. Here is how to hold it honestly.
body:
I came to faith from atheism, which means I know the inside of unbelief, and I know that the church often handles doubt in the worst possible way, by treating it as a sin to be repented of rather than a question to be honored. So the doubter learns to hide. He sits in the pew performing a certainty he does not feel, terrified that if he says the true thing out loud he will be corrected, pitied, or quietly written off. Let me say the freeing thing first. Doubt is not the enemy of faith. Handled honestly, it is often the road to a faith that can actually bear weight.

## Distinguish your doubts from your faith

The first mistake is to treat doubt as total, to feel one question and conclude the whole thing is collapsing. It is not. You can have a real doubt about a specific thing, the problem of suffering, a hard text, the silence of God, while the larger structure still stands. Name the actual doubt. Get specific. "I doubt that a good God would allow this" is a real, workable question. "I doubt everything" is usually just fear in a trench coat. Specific doubts can be examined. Vague dread cannot.

## Take your doubts to God, not just about him

You do not have to leave the room to doubt. The father in Mark cried out, "I believe; help my unbelief," and that contradiction, faith and doubt in the same breath, is one of the most honest prayers in the Bible, and Jesus answered it. Thomas doubted the resurrection out loud, refused to believe without evidence, and Jesus did not condemn him. He showed him his hands. Bring your doubts to God himself. Pray your questions. A God who can be questioned is a God strong enough to be trusted.

## Do the work of actually looking for answers

Some doubts persist simply because we never investigate them. We carry a half-formed objection for years and never read the people who have thought about it deeply. The Christian tradition is not afraid of hard questions, and it has been answering them for two thousand years. Read. Ask the pastor the real question. Find the thinkers, ancient and modern, who have wrestled with your exact objection. Faith is not a refusal to think. It has nothing to fear from honest inquiry, and much to gain.

## Sit with the doubts that do not resolve

Some questions will not be answered, and a mature faith makes peace with that. Job demanded an explanation for his suffering and never got one. God answered him not with reasons but with himself, with a presence so overwhelming that the questions, while never answered, were somehow no longer the point. There is a kind of trust that holds the unanswered question and keeps walking anyway, not because it has solved the mystery but because it has come to trust the One inside it.

## Do not let doubt make its decisions in the dark

Doubt loves isolation and the small hours. Do not let it deliberate alone. Tell a trusted believer, a pastor, a friend whose faith has scars on it. Stay in the community even when you feel like a fraud there. And whatever you do, do not make a permanent decision about faith in a temporary season of darkness or grief, when your judgment is least reliable. Doubt that is spoken aloud and walked through with others rarely ends where it started.

**This week:** Write down the one doubt that troubles you most, the real one, in a single honest sentence. Then do two things. Bring it to God in prayer, out loud, exactly as you wrote it. And bring it to one trusted person who will not flinch, and ask them to think about it with you. Do not carry it alone in the dark any longer.

Doubt that is hidden festers. Doubt that is honored, examined, prayed, and shared has a way of becoming the doorway to a deeper faith, the kind that has looked into the abyss and chosen God anyway, not out of naivety but with eyes open. The opposite of faith was never doubt. The opposite of faith is indifference, and the fact that you are still wrestling means you still care, and the fact that you still care means it is not over.
